To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IOLs we studied increased the relative intensity and area of surface reflections when compared with the human crystalline eye, and that the IOL designs with an anterior optic radius of curvature of less than 17.0mm minimized surface reflections.
all IOLs increase internal and external surface reflection compared to the unaccommodating crystalline lens, and the magnitude of this increase depends on the design of the IOL.
surface reflections from IOLs are more intense than those of the human crystalline and are minimized with an anterior surface radius of curvature of 17.0mm or less.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between intraocular lens (IOL) surface designs and the amount of surface reflections in the postoperative eye.
the design of the intraocular lens and its relationship to postoperative surface reflections.
the relationship of the optical design of IOLs to the amount and location of surface reflections in the human eye.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all of the IOLs in our study increased the relative intensity and area of surface reflections compared to the human lens.

all IOLs studied have increased surface reflections when compared with the unaccommodating human lens, but the AcrySof MA60BM and SA30AL IOLs have the least surface reflections of all the IOL designs studied.
the design of an optic surface is important to minimize surface reflections, but the effect of the optic design is only one component of the overall effect on surface reflections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

surface reflections are a significant problem in all the IOL models studied and that the surface reflections are reduced in the SA30AL and the MA60BM IOLs, which have a central anterior optic surface radius of curvature of 8.0 and 8.6 mm, respectively.
all the intraocular lenses studied increased the potential for surface reflected glare, and that the design of the anterior surface of the optic is the major contributor.

the surface reflections from the anterior surface of a spherical optic with a 17 mm radius of curvature is about 10‐fold less intense than from the posterior surface of a spherical lens of the same radius of curvature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface reflections are not a function of IOL material but of optic design.
the surface reflections are a function of the radius of curvature of the anterior surface of the IOL optic.
the surface design of the IOL optic can be a significant factor in the amount of surface reflections that may be experienced by the patient.
